$comment: Canonical registry of EXTERNAL tools this catalog points at but does NOT bundle. No third-party source code is vendored in this repository — each entry is a pointer plus the metadata an agent needs to evaluate, install, and invoke the tool. This file is the source of truth: README and any pointer skill must agree with it, and CI enforces that the pinned sourceRef matches.

tools.name: osti-axi
tools.description: OSTI.GOV search and full-text retrieval CLI for agents. Searches DOE-funded research records, returns compact TOON output, and saves OSTI-provided PDF/text artifacts into the agent's workspace. Read-only: it never publishes, edits, or submits to OSTI, and never extracts text from PDFs.

notes: Upstream has no git tags, no GitHub releases, and is not published to npm, so a commit SHA is the only immutable locator. The pin above was installed and smoke-tested end-to-end on 2026-09-22.

Do NOT install via 'npm install -g git+https://...#<sha>'. The package declares a 'prepack' script but no 'prepare' script, so npm does not build dist/ for git-spec installs and the declared bin target ./dist/bin/osti-axi.js never exists.

The upstream README's install snippet (clone then 'npm install -g .') is also insufficient from a clean clone: without a prior 'npm install' and 'npm run build' the TypeScript is never compiled and no binary is produced. The steps above are the verified-working sequence.
'npm install -g' places a binary on the user's PATH. Treat this as third-party code execution and obtain explicit user consent first.

commands.name: search
commands.summary: Search OSTI records by keyword and/or fielded filters.

commands.name: digest
commands.summary: Fetch one record with abstract and resource links.

commands.name: download
commands.summary: Save OSTI-provided PDF/text artifacts. Writes to ./osti-downloads/ by default.

verified.method: Installed from the pinned commit into a throwaway npm prefix, confirmed 'osti-axi --version' reported 0.1.0, and ran a live read-only search against OSTI.GOV.

tools.name: hullrad-axi
tools.description: Hydrodynamic property estimation from a PDB or mmCIF structure for agents. Wraps an unmodified copy of HullRad 10.2 and returns compact TOON output — amino-acid count, molecular mass, and translational/rotational diffusion coefficients and radii. Read-only with respect to the input structure: it never mutates or uploads the caller's coordinates, and it performs no network calls after installation.
tools.licenseNotes: The AXI wrapper is MIT (PNNL). The bundled HullRadV10.2.py is Patrick Fleming's, dedicated to the public domain under the Unlicense. See THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md upstream. Cite Fleming & Fleming, Biophysical Journal 114 (2018) 856-869, doi:10.1016/j.bpj.2018.01.002 when reporting results.

runtimePrerequisites.python: not required on the host — the postinstall script provisions Python 3.11 in an isolated environment via a pinned uv download from Astral

notes: Upstream has no git tags, no GitHub releases, and is not published to npm, so a commit SHA is the only immutable locator. The '#<sha>' suffix on the package spec is what pins the install; without it npm resolves the default branch, which moves.
'--install-links' makes npm copy the GitHub package instead of linking a temporary checkout. Omitting it leaves the global bin pointing at a checkout npm may reclaim.

'--allow-scripts' explicitly permits this package's postinstall Python setup script so npm does not warn about an unreviewed lifecycle script. That script downloads uv from Astral and provisions Python 3.11 — it is real third-party code execution with network egress, so obtain explicit user consent first.
'npm install -g' places a binary on the user's PATH. Uninstall with 'npm uninstall -g hullrad-axi'.
Structures are caller-supplied; the package ships no sample PDB/mmCIF files. 'hullrad-axi doctor --structure <file>' is the end-to-end smoke test.
Set AXI_PYTHON to override the provisioned interpreter. Any override must already have NumPy and SciPy.

commands.name: doctor
commands.summary: Check the bundled engine and provisioned Python environment; with --structure, run a full calculation as an end-to-end test.

commands.name: inspect
commands.summary: Report a structure's path, format, size, SHA-256, and PDB coordinate-record count. Does not run HullRad.

commands.name: fields
commands.summary: List every result key accepted by --fields, marking defaults and the native HullRad label.

commands.name: run
commands.summary: Calculate one structure. --out-dir preserves an input snapshot, native logs, normalized results, and a JSON manifest.

commands.name: batch
commands.summary: Run several structures in sequence, writing a separate record per structure under a new --out-dir.

verified.method: METADATA ONLY — the install steps above have NOT been executed end-to-end. The pinned commit was cloned and read (package.json bin/engines/postinstall, README command surface, LICENSE, THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md), and every field here was derived from that tree. 'verify' and 'verifyExpect' come from the upstream README and package.json version, not from an observed run. Re-verify by installing into a throwaway npm prefix and running 'hullrad-axi doctor --structure <file>' before relying on this entry.
